issues.legal_issue: Property allotted to a family member in a family partition to discharge family debts becomes that member’s separate property when the allotment is consideration for a personal undertaking to bear the debt risk and the arrangement is bona fide and fair.
material_facts: A partition deed allotted specified family properties to one member, who undertook sole responsibility for discharging specified family debts irrespective of whether the properties were sufficient.
The other family members were relieved of responsibility for those debts, and any surplus or deficit was to be enjoyed or borne by the member who undertook to pay them.
The deed gave that member exclusive possession and enjoyment of the properties in consideration of the undertaking.
The arrangement was found to be bona fide and fair.
issues.conclusion: The allotted properties became the member’s separate properties from the execution of the partition deed and were not liable to partition.
issues.legal_principle: In a family partition, the family must account for both assets and debts. Bona fide family arrangements made to maintain peace or harmony should be sustained where their terms are fair in the circumstances (Sahu Madho Das v. Pandit Mukand Ram; Maturi Pullaiah v. Maturi Narasimham; S. Shanmugam Pillai v. K. Shanmugam Pillai). An allotment made in return for a member’s personal undertaking to discharge debts, with exclusive responsibility for any deficit and enjoyment of any surplus, is in the nature of remuneration and may be that member’s separate property; the Court also referred to Raj Kumar Singh Kukam Chandji v. Commissioner of Income-tax, Madhya Pradesh, on remuneration as individual income.

rule.if: family_partition_proceeding and debt_discharge_undertaking and exclusive_debt_risk and bona_fide_fair_arrangement

predicates.family_partition_proceeding: The dispute arises in a proceeding seeking division of family property.
predicates.debt_discharge_undertaking: A family member undertook personal responsibility for discharging family debts in return for an allotment of property.
predicates.exclusive_debt_risk: The member’s responsibility for the debts was independent of the sufficiency of the allotted property, and the member was to enjoy any surplus or bear any deficit.
predicates.bona_fide_fair_arrangement: The family arrangement was made bona fide and its terms were fair in the circumstances.

issues.definition: When a partition proceeding concerns a bona fide and fair allotment made for a member’s personal undertaking to discharge family debts while bearing any deficit and enjoying any surplus, the allotted property is separate and not partitionable.

issues.legal_issue: A member’s separate property does not become joint family property by blending unless the member clearly intends to abandon the separate rights in it.
material_facts: The property had been allotted to the member as his separate property.
There was no evidence that he intended to abandon his separate rights in the property.
He had not entered the property separately in account books or maintained separate accounts for its earnings.
issues.conclusion: The property did not become joint family property; the absence of separate entries or accounts did not alter its separate character.
issues.legal_principle: Separate property may be impressed with the character of joint family property when its owner voluntarily throws it into the common stock with a clear intention to abandon separate rights. That intention is a question of fact and cannot be inferred merely from physical mixing, family members’ joint use, generosity in applying income, or failure to maintain separate accounts (Lakkireddi Chinna Venkata Reddi v. Lakkireddi Lakshmama; G. Narayana Ram v. G. Chamaraju).

predicates.partition_proceeding: The dispute arises in a proceeding seeking division of family property.
predicates.separately_owned_property: The property was held by a family member as separate property before the alleged blending.
predicates.no_clear_abandonment_intent: The owner did not clearly intend to give up separate rights in the property.

issues.definition: In a partition proceeding, separately owned property retains its separate character when its owner did not clearly intend to abandon separate rights in it.

issues.legal_issue: A coparcener seeking partition cannot demand an account of a family manager’s past dealings with family property without proof of misappropriation or fraudulent or improper conversion.
material_facts: A coparcener seeking partition claimed that the former family manager should account for past dealings with family property.
There was no evidence that the former manager had misappropriated or fraudulently or improperly converted family property.
The dispute concerned the manager’s dealings before partition was demanded.
issues.conclusion: The former manager was not liable to account for past dealings; the coparcener was entitled to an account of the joint family property as it existed when partition was demanded.
issues.legal_principle: In the absence of proof of misappropriation or fraudulent or improper conversion by a joint family manager, a coparcener seeking partition cannot require an account of the manager’s past dealings and is entitled only to an account of the joint family property existing when partition is demanded.

predicates.partition_proceeding: The dispute arises in a proceeding in which a coparcener seeks partition.
predicates.past_family_manager_dealings: The requested account concerns a manager’s completed dealings with family property before partition was demanded.
predicates.no_proof_of_misappropriation_or_improper: There is no proof that the manager misappropriated or fraudulently or improperly converted family property.

issues.definition: When a coparcener seeks partition and there is no proof of misappropriation or fraudulent or improper conversion, the coparcener cannot require an account of the manager’s past dealings.

issues.legal_issue: The use of joint family funds to discharge family debts does not change the separate character of property allotted to a member, although the member’s legal representatives are liable for the amounts so used.
material_facts: Specified property had been allotted to a member as his separate property in return for his undertaking to discharge family debts.
Some joint family funds were also used to discharge those debts.
The legal representatives of the member who received the allotment were parties to the dispute.
issues.conclusion: Use of joint family funds did not affect the separate character of the allotted property, but the member’s legal representatives were liable for the amounts of joint family funds used to pay the debts.
issues.legal_principle: The use of joint family funds to discharge debts does not alter the character of property separately allotted in a valid family arrangement; the recipients’ legal representatives remain liable for the joint family funds used.

predicates.partition_proceeding: The dispute arises in a proceeding concerning division of family property.
predicates.separate_property_allocation: A family member received property as separate property under an arrangement for discharging family debts.
predicates.joint_family_funds_used_for_debts: Some joint family funds were used to discharge those debts.

issues.definition: When joint family funds are used to discharge debts associated with a separate property allocation, the property retains its character and the recipient’s legal representatives are liable for the funds used.
